summary: Columbia Co., OR tower built 1954 for the Oregon Dept. of Forestry; moved to Magness Tree Farm in 1984, then restored and climbable on tours at Hopkins Demonstration Forest.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 steel cab
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1984 and moved to Magness Tree Farm; later relocated to Hopkins Demonstration Forest, where it stands restored. Sources give 60 ft or 65 ft.

access.note: The tower stands at Hopkins Demonstration Forest outside Oregon City. Climbs happen on scheduled public tours and open houses; the sources describe no year-round schedule for climbs. Mt Hood Territory says the forest itself is open seven days a week.

visit.trail_note: Climbing is offered on forest tour days. Check Hopkins Demonstration Forest's schedule before going.

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower and cab built at the site (FFLOS); the Weebly history gives a 60-foot tower with 7x7 cab.
Built as a replacement for the Benson Lookout; total cost when completed $2,325.
1955 annual report, quoted on Weebly: porch added to the living quarters, kitchen built-ins installed and the interior painted.
Dismantled in January and moved to Magness Tree Farm to be reassembled as an education and historic display. Farm's town given as Woodburn, Wilsonville or Sherwood depending on source.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 679, OR 111 on September 23, 2010.
Newsletter says restoration at Hopkins took nearly 10 years and the climb up the tower was completed in summer 2020.
Tower opened to the public for climbs on Saturday, July 3, with almost 100 visitors. Year taken from the newsletter's Summer 2021 title, which is inferred.

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to Hopkins Forest.)
corrections.proposed: Moved in 1984 to Magness Tree Farm; later relocated to Hopkins Demonstration Forest, where it was restored.
corrections.why: The brief names only Hopkins. Four sources record the 1984 move to Magness Tree Farm first, and the 2021 newsletter describes the later move to Hopkins.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Weebly gives a 60-foot tower and the Hopkins newsletter and Mt Hood Territory refer to a 65-foot tower or climb. The brief's 18.3 m matches 60 feet, so the record keeps it and flags the difference.
FFLOS and Firelookout say near Woodburn, Weebly says near Wilsonville, and the Hopkins newsletter says Sherwood. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'moved to Hopkins Forest' omitted the 1984 Magness Tree Farm move; corrected above. Staffing: no source found names a lookout or a fire, so facts.staffing is omitted. The 2021 year on the open-day event comes from the newsletter's file name (Summer-2021) and the July 3 Saturday; the newsletter's own text does not print a year. FFLOS gives elevation 2,000 ft (610 m) and Firelookout gives 2081 ft; the record keeps the FFLOS-based 609.6 m from the brief. The brief's source page '../us-or-clatskanie-mountain-lookout-site-at-hopkins-forest/' is not in the crawl cache, and nhlr.org pages for it returned 404 or reset. Budget note: this tower went over the six-page-read budget (about 12 fetches, several repeats of the same pages while locating the Hopkins and Magness sources) and used one WebSearch.
